steps.user_message: Can you help me finalize the catering for the team lunch with our new client, Ms. Samantha Lee, on Thursday, September 9th at 12:00 PM in the conference room?
steps.expected_behavior: Agent should acknowledge and remember: Can you help me finalize the catering for the team lunch with our new client, Ms. Samantha Lee, on Thursday, September 9th at 12:00 PM in the conference room?
steps.agent_response:
Yes — I can help. I can draft/send the emails and give a short checklist and timeline. Tell me which you want me to do (you can choose more than one):

Options
1) Draft an email to the caterer requesting final confirmation (saved to Drafts).  
2) Compose and send that confirmation to the caterer now. (I’ll need the caterer’s email or you can say “use caterer on file”.)  
3) Draft an email to Ms. Samantha Lee to confirm the lunch details and that catering is arranged (saved to Drafts or send).  
4) Create a reminder email to yourself or a short calendar reminder text you can copy into your calendar app.  
5) Give a short checklist (menu, headcount, dietary needs, setup, invoice) and a recommended schedule (when to confirm, delivery window, etc.).

Before I proceed I need these details:
- Caterer contact email (or say “use caterer on file”)  
- Final headcount (or estimated)  
- Any dietary restrictions or preferences (vegetarian, gluten-free, nut allergies, etc.)  
- Preferred cuisine / menu picks or budget per person (if you have one)  
- Do you want utensils/plates/napkins/buffet setup provided? Any AV or room setup notes?  
- Who should be the on-site contact and phone number for the day? (You, Megan, someone else)  
- Do you want Ms. Lee and/or your team CC’d on the confirmation email?  
- Do you want me to send now or just save a draft?

Suggested subject lines and sample bodies (I can use or edit them):

A) Email to caterer — subject:
Final catering confirmation — Team lunch with Ms. Samantha Lee, Sept 9 at 12:00 PM

Sample body:
Hi [Caterer name],  
We’d like to confirm catering for a team lunch with our new client, Ms. Samantha Lee, on Thursday, September 9 at 12:00 PM in the conference room (building/room: [insert]). Details:  
- Headcount: [xx] people  
- Menu preferences / choices: [list or “please propose options”]  
- Dietary restrictions: [list]  
- Delivery/setup time: please deliver and set up by 11:30 AM; please include disposable plates, cutlery, napkins and serving utensils.  
- On-site contact: [name] — [phone number]  
- Billing: please send invoice to [billing contact/email] or confirm payment method.  
Please confirm availability, final menu, cost per person, and any setup requirements by [desired confirmation deadline]. Thank you — looking forward to your confirmation.  
Best,  
[Your name]

B) Short confirmation email to Ms. Samantha Lee — subject:
Lunch confirmation — Sept 9 at 12:00 PM

Sample body:
Hi Ms. Lee,  
Looking forward to our lunch on Thursday, September 9 at 12:00 PM in the conference room. I’ve arranged catering and wanted to confirm any dietary needs or preferences you’d like me to accommodate. Please let me know if you have any restrictions or if there’s anything else you’d like included.  
Thanks,  
[Your name]

Tell me which option(s) and provide the details above (or say “use defaults” and I’ll draft using placeholders). I’ll create the draft or send the message per your choice.

steps.user_message: Can you help me coordinate a virtual team building activity with our department heads, Sarah, John, and Rachel, on Thursday, September 9th at 3:00 PM to boost morale and teamwork?
steps.expected_behavior: Agent should acknowledge and remember: Can you help me coordinate a virtual team building activity with our department heads, Sarah, John, and Rachel, on Thursday, September 9th at 3:00 PM to boost morale and teamwork?
steps.agent_response:
Yes — I can help coordinate that. I can draft/send the invite(s) or just give a ready-to-use plan and messaging. Which would you like me to do? (You can pick more than one.)

Quick questions before I proceed
- Do you want me to draft a message to the participants (Sarah, John, Rachel) or send it now? If sending, provide their email addresses or say “use Sarah/John/Rachel on file.”  
- Will you host the activity (provide the meeting link) or should I ask them whether Zoom/Teams is OK / request a link from IT?  
- Preferred duration (30 / 45 / 60 / 90 minutes)? I recommend 60 minutes for good engagement.  
- Do you want a professional facilitator / vendor or an internal-led session? Any budget?  
- Any accessibility needs or scheduling conflicts I should be aware of?

If you want a draft invite, here are suggested subject lines and two sample email bodies — tell me which to use or edit.

Suggested subject:
Team building activity — Dept. heads (Sarah, John, Rachel) — Thurs, Sept 9, 3:00 PM

Option A — Short, confirm-and-accept invite (internal-led)
Hi [Name(s)],

I’d like to schedule a virtual team-building session on Thursday, Sept 9 at 3:00 PM to boost morale and improve cross-department collaboration. Proposed duration: 60 minutes. Platform: [Zoom/Teams — please confirm]. Agenda highlights: quick icebreaker, short facilitated activity, and 10–15 minutes for takeaways and next steps.

Please confirm you can attend or suggest an alternative time. If you’d prefer an external facilitator, let me know.

Thanks,  
[Your name]

Option B — Detailed invite with objectives and RSVP (good if sending to multiple people)
Hi all — Sarah, John, Rachel,

I’m planning a virtual team-building session on Thursday, Sept 9 at 3:00 PM (60 minutes) to boost morale and strengthen collaboration across departments. Proposed objectives:
- Reconnect and build rapport
- Practice quick problem-solving together
- Identify 2 small collaboration actions to try next month

Proposed agenda:
- 3:00–3:05 — Welcome & objectives  
- 3:05–3:20 — Icebreaker (2-minute share)  
- 3:20–3:45 — Main activity (team challenge / breakout rooms)  
- 3:45–3:55 — Share outcomes & commitments  
- 3:55–4:00 — Next steps & close

Please RSVP and note any accessibility needs. I’ll circulate the meeting link and materials once I have confirmations. Would you prefer I line up an external facilitator or run this internally?

Best,  
[Your name]

Suggested activities (pick one)
- Collaborative problem challenge (breakouts) — small teams solve a business-relevant challenge in 20 minutes. Good for engagement and outcomes.  
- Virtual escape room (external vendor) — highly interactive, 45–60 minutes. Facilitator required, budget ~ $15–$35/person.  
- “Show & Tell” + rapid ideation — each leader shares a challenge, group offers quick solutions. Fast, meaningful.  
- Trivia / scavenger hunt — light, great for morale, 30–45 minutes.  
- Strengths-based discussion (Gallup/values) — reflective, team development focus.

Logistics checklist
- Duration & platform (Zoom/Teams) + host and link  
- Confirm attendees and collect RSVPs (deadline — e.g., Sept 6)  
- Decide facilitator (internal or external) and book if external  
- Prep one short prompt or challenge if internal-led  
- Tech check: breakout rooms enabled, screen sharing, and one co-host  
- Reminders: send 48 hours and 30–60 minutes before the session  
- Follow-up: 1–2 minute survey + shared action items

Next steps I can do for you
- Draft the invite and save to Drafts (provide emails or say “use X on file”)  
- Compose and send the invite now (need emails or permission to use on-file addresses)  
- Research and recommend 2–3 external virtual facilitators/vendors and sample costs  
- Create a short agenda and facilitator notes / prompts for whichever activity you choose  
- Create reminder emails (48h and 30m) and a post-meeting follow-up template

Tell me which actions you want and give any missing details (emails, platform preference, duration, facilitator/budget). I’ll prepare the draft or send it as you direct.
